compactMembership.notes: Texas's electrician reciprocity operates via named bilateral agreements with individual states, not a single multistate compact license practiced across member states without a new license (the defining feature of a true compact). Recorded as false to avoid conflating these bilateral agreements with a compact under this field's actual schema meaning.

reciprocityRules.value: Texas has confirmed Master Electrician reciprocity agreements with: Arkansas, Nebraska, North Carolina, Louisiana (subject to a special residency condition — see below), Iowa, Alabama, and Ohio. Iowa-Master was confirmed via an official TDLR press release dated 2026-02-05, even though the primary out-of-state.htm listing page had not yet been updated to include it at time of research. Alabama-Master was confirmed via an official TDLR announcement (~2026-03-20). Ohio-Master was confirmed via an official TDLR announcement (June 2026).

requiredDocuments.value: A letter of good standing from the issuing state's licensing authority, confirming the applicant passed the statewide electrical exam, holds a current Master Electrician license, and is in good standing. For Louisiana specifically, the applicant must additionally be a Louisiana resident to qualify.
